beats.subline: Friday, July 31, 2026 close — broad gains closed out a strong July as Amazon's earnings beat offset rising bond yields.
beats.body: Amazon's stronger-than-expected earnings and cloud growth drove a roughly 15% jump in its shares, powering all three indexes to gains on the last trading day of July even as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since early 2025.

beats.headline: Trump halts planned attack on Iran, citing progress toward a rapid deal
beats.body: Trump said Saturday night the US is canceling a planned strike on Iran after Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked him to hold off, with a proposed deal calling for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear weapons program; Israel has agreed to join the pause, and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had separately pushed Trump toward de-escalation.

beats.headline: Taiwan tracks two Chinese coast guard ships east of the island as patrols continue
beats.body: Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration said Saturday it deployed the patrol ship Taipei to monitor two China Coast Guard vessels, the Xiushan and Chongming, operating east of Lanyu island, part of a patrol pattern Beijing has maintained since June; Taipei accused Beijing of "fake law enforcement, real expansion of power" and vowed to defend the nation's sovereignty.

beats.headline: US forces stay at heightened alert in the Gulf as Iran strike pause holds
beats.body: No new US strikes on Iran have been reported since Wednesday's "heavy wave" of attacks, but CENTCOM continues enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports and US forces remain on heightened alert across the region while the pause holds; the State Department is urging American citizens in the Middle East to consider departing.

beats.headline: Bears close out fourth camp practice with a Williams-to-Odunze two-minute score
beats.body: Chicago practiced without pads for a fourth straight day Saturday, moving indoors for lightning before a Caleb Williams-to-Rome Odunze fade-route touchdown capped a two-minute drill; undrafted rookie receiver JP Richardson kept turning heads with more highlight catches in 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 work.
